title: Reuse existing enterprise Wi-Fi profiles on reconnect
head: fa93778d610f
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: CAT EAP-TLS profiles require a different secret than the reused-profile editor writes
leads.consequence: On a CAT-installed wpa-eap profile configured for EAP-TLS with an unavailable or wrong private-key password, the inline retry writes 802-1x.password, not 802-1x.private-key-password. The matched profile remains and repeated attempts cannot repair that missing key password. This is a boundary of the reuse-by-SSID/key-mgmt predicate, not a failure of profile matching. PEAP/TTLS password-based profiles are distinct and should not be generalized to TLS. The CLI's failure is not used to choose a different secret field.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up Q1 confirmed (source + stub); published within N2 with agent-owned qualifier

leads.summary: Only new enterprise profiles lose the old 8-second auth timeout; reused legacy profiles keep it until #12279's migration
leads.consequence: A profile created by the old panel with 802-1x.auth-timeout=8 enters the reuse branch, which updates identity/password but leaves the old 8-second override untouched. #12279 separately migrates the same profiles to 0; its Model.js change conflicts textually with this PR, so an integration should retain this PR's reuse plus its migration (not merely the now-0 new-profile line). This affects slow existing enterprise connections even if the new join path succeeds.
leads.triage: already in prior public R1 and Opus final; corroborated; published as unchanged status

leads.summary: Failed retry on an existing profile preserves its UUID but overwrites its previous credentials
leads.consequence: If an existing profile has a valid old password/identity and a user enters new credentials during a temporary AP/RADIUS outage, the editor saves the replacement before connection up fails. The cleanup checks created=0, so it retains the now-changed profile, not the old working configuration. Subsequent autoconnects use the replacement until the user repairs it outside this flow. The failure test seeds no previous password and checks only that the profile file survives, missing this state change.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up Q2 confirmed (stub run 20260928T053607Z-5e9d1ab2 + NM source); published as N2

leads.summary: WPA3 Enterprise 192-bit is absent from the new enterprise-failure classifier
leads.consequence: Quickshell emits WifiSecurityType.Wpa3SuiteB192 for an EAP Suite-B-192 AP. The changed isEnterpriseSecurity() returns false, so a credentialed WifiAuthTimeout still says Wrong password instead of the head's enterprise Connection timed out. On an unknown network, the existing credential submit branch additionally uses connectWithPsk, so do not infer that changing the label alone enables joining these networks. Test only covers Wpa2Eap/WpaEap flag passed directly, not the real producer enum.
leads.triage: factual, verified (Suite-B not classified enterprise); dropped: matches pre-existing row classification, timeout branch unreachable, rare

leads.summary: The open cancellation PR has a conflicting unconditional delete for the reused-profile branch
leads.consequence: These PRs are diverged and their script hunks conflict. #13088's TERM trap invokes drop(), which unconditionally deletes $u, while this PR's $u can refer to a CAT-installed profile. An integration that preserves #13088's trap unchanged would delete the institutional profile on Cancel; an integration choosing this PR alone has no cancellation handling. Resolve deliberately by tracking ownership in the TERM handler and guarding deletion with created. This is an integration hazard, not a claim GitHub automatically combined them.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator in intake/pr-13088.diff (drop() deletes $u unconditionally); published in Related

leads.summary: New reuse fixture passes even when connection edit never saves the requested secret
leads.consequence: The stub writes profile fields on set and ignores save/quit. A mutant of Model.js that removes the save command still passes every case in this new test (including reuse, create and failures), though real nmcli's editor only commits changes in its SAVE branch. This means the fixture cannot detect a plausible regression that leaves the old password and identity in the reused profile. Make the stub stage edits in memory and persist on save, asserting the saved fields before activation.
leads.triage: factual, stub source verified (save no-op); not published: test-only on earlier-round code, kept proportionate; recorded in REPORT

leads.summary: The nmcli editor persists submitted 802.1X passwords in its command-history cache
leads.consequence: Even though the password does not appear in argv, the script types `set 802-1x.password <secret>` into nmcli's interactive editor. nmcli adds every nonempty stdin line to readline history and writes that history, indexed by UUID, to the user's nmcli-history cache on quit. Thus saved reused profiles leave a second plaintext copy of each submitted credential outside NetworkManager; this path also existed for newly synthesized profiles in the base, so this is a persisting security boundary, not newly introduced solely by these commits.
leads.triage: pre-existing on base, not a regression; dropped; recorded in REPORT

leads.summary: First direct attempt on a known but secret-less network now labels NoSecrets as Wrong password
leads.consequence: A saved protected profile may exist without an available secret (CAT agent-owned password after a reboot with no agent, or a PSK profile with no stored PSK). Clicking that known row calls connect() without asking for a password. If NetworkManager fails with NoSecrets, the head's changed mapping displays Wrong password in the retry prompt even though no password was submitted during this action; the earlier mapping said Passphrase required. This is a copy-state distinction, not evidence that a submitted wrong password should lose its Wrong password message.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (caveat a); published as one sentence

limits: No physical Wi-Fi / NetworkManager execution: all daemon-dependent outcomes use upstream 1.58.1 / Quickshell v0.3.1 source and a fully stubbed nmcli fixture; CAT source snapshot fd164116 is current upstream master, not an institution-specific installed installer. Do not infer every CAT installation has missing secrets.

The failed first exploratory run under review.py (plan/runs/20260928T051559Z-7e4db99d) was a fixture path-assertion error; plan3/runs/20260928T051909Z-5b13df63 failed to locate the mutation token. Neither is evidence of PR failure. Subsequent plan2 and plan4 receipts verify successfully.

flags.claim: This refines the previous review, whose suggestions considered only the timeout reason for enterprise networks.
flags.why: The previous review (comment 5856397312) tabulated 'NoSecrets (PSK or enterprise)' and suggested keeping 'Wrong password' for a NoSecrets reprompt after a submitted passphrase; the author implemented exactly that. Its Impact paragraph also discussed enterprise NO_SECRETS. This round's suggestion (neutral text for enterprise NoSecrets) revises that advice for enterprise networks rather than filling a gap.

flags.claim: Supply the password only for the activation, for example through nmcli's passwd-file from a file descriptor, instead of saving it before connection up.
flags.why: passwd-file only reaches NetworkManager through nmcli's secret agent, and NetworkManager asks agents only when the profile's system-owned secrets are insufficient. For a password-flags=0 profile that already stores a password, activation completes the secrets request from the stored password and never asks the agent, so the typed password would be ignored. The remedy fits agent-owned (password-flags=1, CAT PEAP/TTLS) or password-less profiles; for flags-0 profiles the stored password still has to be updated (with restore on failure). My own follow-up answer offered passwd-file without this caveat.

flags.claim: Limit reuse to profiles whose 802-1x.eap is peap or ttls, and leave other methods untouched.
flags.why: Part of the suggestion was dropped. With the current helper, a skipped EAP-TLS profile leaves $u empty and the helper synthesizes a new minimal PEAP/MSCHAPv2 profile without CA checks for the same SSID, which is the #11791 risk the PR exists to avoid. My follow-up said to neither write nor synthesize in that case.

flags.claim: Retries from the panel cannot succeed there
flags.why: Lost qualifier. Retries cannot succeed only while the TLS key password is unavailable to NetworkManager (agent-owned, as CAT installs it, with no secret agent running). If the key password is stored (flags 0) or an agent supplies it, the retry can connect; the typed password is irrelevant but the identity is still rewritten.

flags.claim: Enterprise failures, including a slow RADIUS round trip, arrive as NoSecrets and read "Wrong password", as on the base branch.
flags.why: They arrive as NoSecrets (source), but the text depends on timing. A reused enterprise profile that has connected before retries with its stored password for up to three auth timeouts (default 3 retries, 25 s each with auth-timeout 0), so NO_SECRETS may arrive after the panel's 30 s timer; the prompt then shows "Timed out connecting" and the late NoSecrets is ignored. On base, the inline text was hard-coded "Wrong password" in both cases. Source-derived, untested (my report HY1).

flags.claim: Test scope: base, previous-head and head test scripts
flags.why: My runs executed the head and previous-head test scripts, plus the head tests against the previous and base Model.js/Panel.qml. I did not run the base branch's own test scripts. If nobody else did, the wording goes beyond the evidence.

flags.claim: an agent-owned one (password-flags=1, as CAT installs PEAP/TTLS) is only cached in memory
flags.why: Minor lost qualifier: NetworkManager caches it in memory and also hands it to any running secret agent to save. With no agent (Omarchy default) it is only cached.

flags.claim: A wrong PSK and an SAE mismatch also end as NO_SECRETS.
flags.why: Nitpick: true when no secret agent supplies a new key, which the code block above states for the timeout path but this sentence does not repeat. With an agent, NetworkManager prompts for a new key.

flags.claim: This round adds two new source-traced findings
flags.why: Nitpick: the unreachable "Connection timed out" text was already raised as an unverified side note in the previous review; this round strengthens it rather than adding it. Line 39 partly acknowledges this.

Enterprise timeout branch effectively unreachable for panel connects; test line 258 pins an unproduced reason; comments misdescribe wrong-PSK reason. comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12889#issuecomment-5856397312) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12889#issuecomment-5857411449), checked at `fa93778d610f`. The `NoSecrets` retry finding is resolved. This round confirms from source an earlier side note, that the enterprise "Connection timed out" text does not appear to be reachable, and adds one new source-traced finding: a failed retry saves the typed credentials into the reused profile. The CAT hypothesis is still untested.

| Earlier item | Status at `fa93778d610f` |
|---|---|
| A `NoSecrets` retry reads "Passphrase required" | Resolved |
| Hypothesis: reused CAT profiles may not receive the typed password | Still unverified; code unchanged, symptom text changed (see below) |
| Reused profiles keep `802-1x.auth-timeout 8` (open #12279) | Unchanged; #12279 is still open |

**Verified:** [Model.js:362](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/fa93778d610f8245c66ce9a865f237216f4c1426/shell/plugins/panels/network/Model.js#L362) maps a credentialed `NoSecrets` failure to "Wrong password" again. A source-derived simulation of the inline prompt (no QML rendering) gives:

```text
NoSecrets on a PSK, SAE or enterprise network   Base             Previous head        Current head
after a submitted passphrase                    Wrong password   Passphrase required  Wrong password
saved network clicked, nothing typed            Wrong password   Passphrase required  Wrong password
```

Both network test scripts pass at head. The updated assertion fails against the previous `Model.js`, and the previous assertion fails against the new one. The earlier fixes (escaped SSID reuse, mapped inline text) are unchanged. Because the mapping is global, a saved network whose password is not stored (for example agent-owned with no secret agent running) also reads "Wrong password" when clicked, as it did on the base branch.

## The enterprise "Connection timed out" text is probably never shown

In the NetworkManager 1.58.1 source, a failed connect to a secured network does not end as a supplicant timeout:

```text
secured infrastructure network, SSID found, association times out
  supplicant_connection_timeout_cb -> handle_auth_or_fail
    no secret agent answers / retries used up -> NO_SECRETS      (Quickshell: NoSecrets)
SUPPLICANT_TIMEOUT only for: ad-hoc/hotspot/mesh, networks with no security setting,
  or link loss after the device is already activated              (Quickshell: WifiAuthTimeout)
```

See `supplicant_connection_timeout_cb` and `link_timeout_cb` in `src/core/devices/wifi/nm-device-wifi.c`. With no secret agent, a wrong PSK and an SAE mismatch also end as `NO_SECRETS`. The panel clears its tracked action once a connect succeeds, so a later link-loss `WifiAuthTimeout` is not treated as its own failure. Omarchy disables iwd, so NetworkManager uses wpa_supplicant. This is source-traced and was not observed at runtime.

**Impact:** the `isEnterprise ? "Connection timed out"` branch ([Model.js:365-366](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/fa93778d610f8245c66ce9a865f237216f4c1426/shell/plugins/panels/network/Model.js#L365-L366)) is not expected to fire for connects started in the panel. Enterprise failures, including a slow RADIUS round trip, arrive as `NoSecrets` and read "Wrong password" when NetworkManager gives up within the panel's 30-second timer, as on the base branch. Later ones show "Timed out connecting". So the PR description's third bullet likely has no visible effect, and the assertion at `test/shell.d/network-test.sh:258` pins a reason that NetworkManager does not produce here. The comments at `Model.js:375-379` and `Panel.qml:997-1002` also say a wrong saved PSK fails with `WifiAuthTimeout`, while the source says `NO_SECRETS`.

**Suggested change:** if the goal of not calling enterprise failures a wrong password stands, give a credentialed enterprise `NoSecrets` neutral text (for example "Authentication failed") and keep "Wrong password" for PSK and SAE. Otherwise drop the timeout branch and that description bullet. This revises the previous review's suggestion, which recommended keeping "Wrong password" for every `NoSecrets` retry, including on enterprise networks.

## A failed retry saves the typed credentials into the reused profile

The helper writes and saves the typed identity and password before activating, and on failure deletes the profile only if it created it ([Model.js:356-358](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/fa93778d610f8245c66ce9a865f237216f4c1426/shell/plugins/panels/network/Model.js#L356-L358)). Results from an nmcli stub with a synthetic existing profile (`identity=stored@uni.example`, `password=stored-good`), a typed `typed@uni.example` / `typo-pass`, and activation made to fail:

```text
                 nmcli calls                                    existing profile afterwards
Base             add <new uuid>, edit, save, up (fails),         unchanged
                 delete <new uuid>
Current head     edit <existing uuid>, save, up (fails)          identity=typed@uni.example
                                                                 password=typo-pass
```

In the NetworkManager source, `save` in `nmcli connection edit` commits the profile persistently. A password with `password-flags=0` is written to the profile's keyfile, while an agent-owned one (`password-flags=1`, as CAT installs PEAP/TTLS) is only cached in memory when no secret agent is running.

The helper also picks any `wpa-eap` profile for the SSID without checking `802-1x.eap`. For an EAP-TLS profile (for example a CAT TLS install), NetworkManager asks only for `802-1x.private-key-password`, so the written `802-1x.password` is never used. When the key password is agent-owned, as CAT installs it, and no secret agent runs, retries from the panel cannot succeed there, and each one replaces the certificate-derived identity.

**Impact:** on a reused profile that stores its password (`password-flags=0`, for example one created by the earlier panel code), a mistyped retry replaces a working password even though the attempt fails. Auto-connect then fails until the correct password is typed again, which may not be possible if the password was provisioned by someone else. The stored identity is replaced on every attempt, including for EAP-TLS profiles. The base branch never modified an existing profile. Only the helper's command order and final state were checked with the stub; NetworkManager's persistence and secret-flag handling are source-traced.

**Suggested change (untested):**
- Limit reuse to profiles whose `802-1x.eap` is `peap` or `ttls`. When the SSID already has an enterprise profile with another method, leave it untouched and do not create a new PEAP profile either.
- For agent-owned passwords (as CAT installs PEAP/TTLS), supply the password only for the activation, for example through nmcli's `passwd-file` from a file descriptor, instead of saving it before `connection up`. This could also address the CAT hypothesis below.
- A profile that stores its password uses the stored one, so there the previous identity and password would need restoring when activation fails.

## Hypothesis unchanged: reused CAT profiles may not receive the typed password

The code path is unchanged since the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12889#issuecomment-5856397312), and a fresh trace of the NetworkManager 1.58.1 source is consistent with it. With the new mapping, if it holds, correct credentials for a reused CAT PEAP/TTLS profile would read "Wrong password" on every attempt instead of "Passphrase required". What would settle it is also unchanged: the PR's unchecked CAT test-plan item, run with no secret agent and credentials known to work.

**Related:** #12279 is still open. Its migration resets the 8-second `auth-timeout` of earlier panel profiles, and its `Model.js` hunk overlaps this PR's. Open #13088 adds a cancel trap to the same helper whose `drop()` deletes `$u` unconditionally. With this PR, `$u` can be a reused institutional profile, so whichever of the two lands second needs to keep the `created` guard on that delete.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** previous-head and head test scripts, and the head tests against the previous and base `Model.js` and `Panel.qml`; a source-derived simulation of the retry prompt; nmcli stub runs of the helper at head and base with synthetic profiles; and NetworkManager 1.58.1, Quickshell 0.3.1, GÉANT CAT installer and open PR #13088 source. No live QML rendering, Wi-Fi hardware, RADIUS server, secret agent or real NetworkManager daemon was exercised.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
